problem:
The following table gives the values of functions $g(x)$ and ${g}^{′}(x)$ at some points. Find $({g}^{-1})^{′}(7).$

| **$x$** | $g(x)$ | ${g}^{′}(x)$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $-6$ | $9$ | $-1$ |
| $4$ | $7$ | $-4$ |
worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of the inverse is

$$
({g}^{-1})^{′}(x)=\frac{1}{{g}^{′}({g}^{-1}(x))}.
$$

Substituting $x=7,$ we have

$$
({g}^{-1})^{′}(7)=\frac{1}{{g}^{′}({g}^{-1}(7))}.
$$

From the table, we obtain ${g}^{-1}(7)=4$ and ${g}^{′}(4)=-4.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}({g}^{-1})^{′}(7) & =\frac{1}{{g}^{′}({g}^{-1}(7))} \\  & =\frac{1}{{g}^{′}(4)} \\  & =\frac{1}{(-4)} \\  & =-\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
